passages.title: The night bus
passages.body: The last bus carried more sound than passengers. A metal panel under the rear seat rattled every time the driver touched the brakes. On Monday, David reported the noise. On Tuesday, when the panel stayed quiet, he found that he had started using its rattle to tell which hill they were on without looking up. He pulled the stop cord one block too soon.

passages.title: Water loss in a window garden
passages.body: Students planted identical seedlings in equal amounts of soil and watered all containers to the same starting mass. They placed four containers near a window and four away from it. Half of each group had a layer of mulch. Each number in the table is the mean loss in container mass after two days. Assume the measured loss came from water leaving the containers.

figure.caption: Mean loss in mass after two days

items: Let $f(x)=3x-4$. Which input gives an output of 11?
Set $3x-4=11$. Add 4 and divide by 3 to get $x=5$.
Work from the inside out. $g(4)=5$, so $f(5)=25+1=26$.
What is the domain of $f(x)=1/(x-5)$ over the real numbers?
The denominator is zero only at $x=5$. Negative denominators are allowed.
The graph of $y=f(x)$ contains the point $(4,-2)$. Which point must be on $y=f(x+3)+5$?
The input to $f$ stays 4 when $x+3=4$, so $x=1$. The new output is $-2+5=3$.
Find the input that produces 19. $4x+7=19$ gives $x=3$.
Subtract 1, then solve $x-2=5$ or $x-2=-5$. The solutions are 7 and −3.
A linear function satisfies $f(2)=9$ and $f(8)=27$. What is $f(0)$?
The slope is $(27-9)/(8-2)=3$. Moving left two units from input 2 lowers the output from 9 to 3.
The parabola is symmetric about $x=3$. The midpoint of $a$ and $a+4$ is $a+2$, so $a+2=3$.
A club sold 18 tickets. Adult tickets cost 9 tokens and student tickets cost 5 tokens. The club collected 122 tokens. How many adult tickets were sold?
Let $a$ count adult tickets. Then $9a+5(18-a)=122$, so $4a+90=122$ and $a=8$.
An isosceles triangle has two equal sides of length 13 and a base of length 10. What is its area?
The altitude divides the base into lengths of 5. Its height is $\sqrt{13^2-5^2}=12$, and the area is $10(12)/2=60$.
The five values 2, 5, 5, 8 and 15 form a data set. If 15 is replaced by 30, what happens to the mean and median?
Mean rises by 3 and median stays the same
Mean stays the same and median rises by 3
The total increases by 15 across five values, so the mean increases by 3. The third value in order stays 5.
A plant increased from 40 cm to 50 cm in height, and then from 50 cm to 60 cm. Which period had the greater percentage increase?
The periods had identical percentage increases
The increases are $10/40=25\%$ and $10/50=20\%$. The first is larger by 5 percentage points.
The fourth root of 16 is 2. Cubing it gives 8.
A tank contains 120 liters at 8:00. Inflow is 9 liters per minute and outflow is 4 liters per minute. How many liters will it contain at 8:14?
The net gain is $9-4=5$ liters per minute, so the tank gains 70 liters in 14 minutes.
Which version keeps the meaning of “The two groups cooperated together to finish the mural” most concisely?
The two groups cooperated to finish the mural.
The two groups both finished the mural together by cooperating.
The two groups finished a pair of murals.
The groups discussed whether to finish the mural.
Cooperated already means worked together. The other concise changes alter the original action or number of murals.
Which revision preserves the meaning of “Because her oven had stopped working, Ada baked the bread at her neighbor’s house”?
Ada baked the bread at her neighbor’s house because her oven broke.
Ada’s neighbor baked the bread when the oven broke.
Ada baked the bread and then went next door.
Ada baked at home after her neighbor’s oven broke.
The first option retains the baker, the alternative location and the reason she used it.
Which wording most concisely replaces “every single member of the group” while preserving its meaning?
Every already includes each member individually. Single is redundant.
Which revision best preserves the meaning of “Before the rehearsal began, Lina returned back to the stage”?
Before rehearsal, Lina returned to the stage.
Lina returned to the stage when rehearsal ended.
Before rehearsal, Lina left the stage again.
Returned includes the idea of going back. Before rehearsal preserves the original timing.
The writer wants readers to know why the paint dried unevenly. Which choice is most concise while keeping the relevant cause?
The paint dried unevenly because a draft cooled one edge of the panel.
One edge of the panel was cooler.
Because of the fact that a draft of air made it cooler on an edge, the panel’s paint dried in an uneven way.
The first option keeps the causal explanation and removes wordy phrases such as “because of the fact that.”
Which revision is most concise while preserving the distinction between two dates in “The club has its weekly meeting on Monday, but the public tour occurs on Friday”?
The club meets weekly and also hosts a tour.
The club meets Mondays, but this week is different.
The club’s weekly meeting is Monday, and the public tour is Friday.
The club meets and gives tours on Mondays and Fridays.
The third choice gives both events and tells readers which day belongs to each.
Which option preserves all the information in “Since fewer people signed up than the organizers expected, they moved the class into a smaller room”?
The organizers moved the class to a smaller room because fewer people signed up than expected.
The organizers moved the class because many people registered.
The small room reduced attendance at the class.
The organizers moved the class into another room for an unknown reason.
Only the first choice keeps the smaller room and the reason for the move: registration fell short of expectations.
Which sentence uses paired commas to set off additional information about an already identified person?
The captain, who had injured her ankle, watched from the bench.
The captain who had injured, her ankle watched from the bench.
The captain who had injured her ankle, watched from the bench.
The captain, who had injured her ankle watched from the bench.
The clause beginning with who is surrounded by commas in the first option. The remaining main clause is complete.
A sentence reports that a community garden doubled its planting area. The next sentence says that it still grew less food during a drought. Which transition best introduces the next sentence?
Nevertheless signals the contrast between the larger area and the lower yield.
Which verb completes the sentence in standard written English? “A set of spare batteries ___ in the drawer.”
The subject is the singular noun set. Of spare batteries modifies set and does not control the verb.
Which verb most precisely conveys that the mechanic examined each connection individually before repairing the radio?
Inspected describes a deliberate examination. The other words do not convey a systematic check.
Why does David most likely pull the cord too early?
The driver deliberately skips a stop.
The quiet bus takes away an unexpected navigation cue.
The driver has changed the route.
David decides to avoid the next hill.
He had been using the rattle to identify hills. Without the rattle, he mistakes where he is on the route.
When did David first report the noise?
Before he ever heard the panel
The third sentence says, “On Monday, David reported the noise.”
What does the final sentence add to the passage?
It explains how the panel was repaired.
It reveals what the driver thought about David.
It shows a practical consequence of the missing sound.
It introduces a new noise that replaces the rattle.
Pulling the cord early shows why losing the noise mattered during David’s ride.
In context, saying the bus “carried more sound than passengers” mainly emphasizes what?
The bus was loud despite having few riders.
The engine sounded like people talking.
The first sentence contrasts the prominent noise with a small number of passengers.
Which choice best states the passage’s central idea?
A passenger comes to depend on a sound he initially found bothersome.
A bus driver invents a better signal to notify riders of hills.
A failed repair leads riders to stop reporting mechanical problems.
A regular rider learns that a faster bus route saves time.
David reports the rattle as a problem, then discovers he had relied on it to track where he was.
Which detail most directly shows that David used the noise as a location cue?
The panel was under the rear seat.
David reported the noise on Monday.
He could tell which hill they were on without looking up.
The last choice directly connects the sound to identifying a specific location.
Which group lost the most water?
Away from the window, with mulch
Away from the window, without mulch
The largest value in the table is 32 g, recorded near the window without mulch.
Which pair isolates the effect of mulch near the window?
Near with mulch and away without mulch
Both near-window groups share the same location. Their mulch treatment is the variable that differs.
How much did mulch reduce the mean mass loss near the window?
At the window, the mean without mulch was 32 g and with mulch was 19 g, a difference of 13 g.
One student says mulch reduces loss by the same amount in both locations. Which evidence directly challenges that claim?
Both locations had equal starting masses.
Without mulch, the window group lost 32 g.
Mulch changed the means by 13 g near the window and 5 g away from it.
The group with the lowest loss was away from the window.
The two measured reductions are different. The other observations do not compare the size of both effects.
Why did the students include two containers in each location-and-mulch combination?
To estimate a mean less sensitive to variation in any one container
To ensure every plant lost the same amount of water
To change two independent variables at once within each combination
To avoid needing a starting mass
Repeating each treatment provides more than one observation and makes its average less affected by an unusual container.
Within the groups with mulch, what was the difference between the window and away means?
Use the with-mulch column. The difference is $19-13=6$ g.
Which change would best test whether results also hold for a different plant species?
Use the new species but place every pot near the window.
Use the new species with twice as much water and compare it with the original study.
Repeat all four treatments with the new species and the same water protocol.
Repeat only the treatment with the smallest observed loss.
Repeating the same four treatments while changing species lets students compare the pattern without changing the test conditions.
One proposed explanation is that the window warmed the soil, increasing water loss. What measurement would most directly help test that explanation?
The soil temperature in both locations during the two days
The cost of a bag of mulch
The number of leaves after six weeks
The length of the window frame
Comparing temperatures in the two locations tests whether the window changed the condition proposed to drive additional loss.
